newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ATHLETICS-ROMANIAN COACH SACKED OVER DOPING CASES.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-ROMANIAN COACH SACKED OVER DOPING CASES.

text.p: The Romanian Athletics Federation (FRA) has sacked Eugen Raducanescu as its national team trainer because of repeated doping cases involving his athletes, the federation's president said on Wednesday.
"Raducanescu was sacked from the technical staff of Romania's national team for repeated proven doping charges against his athletes," FRA president Iolanda Balas told Reuters.
"Four of his athletes, all of them still junior, have been or are still banned from national and international competition."

The federation banned three women in Raducanescu's charge -- Magdalena Nedelcu, Marina Florea and Daniela Bran -- for periods of two to four years after they tested positive for nandrolone, one of the most powerful anabolic steroids in use.
The most celebrated case with Raducanescu's athletes involved Andreea Burlacu, winner of the 400 metres at last year's junior world championships in Sydney, who was banned for two years.

Altogether 11 top Romanian athletes have been banned in the last four years, among them long-distance runner Iulia Negura. Dorin Melinte, who coached Negura and the rest of Romania's long-distance team, resigned in January, saying he could not work in "an atmosphere of suspicion".
Balas said the FRA was determined to stop the use of banned substances.

"We want to clean up doping by all possible means," Balas said. "We'll suspend anyone using even the weakest amphetamines for three months. Any repeat offender proved to have been using anabolic steroids will be suspended for life."
